limitsAndSafetyDifferences: Pinned Pi findMostRecentSession scans at most a 1 MiB header prefix and list streams candidate files. PiSharp discovery imports bounded whole files and rejects files above its 128 MiB import limit; this is a documented resource-safety difference, not a strict match for arbitrarily large sessions.

Configured/shared Pi directories require an explicit nonempty persisted cwd for project-scoped list, findById and recent selection. The PiSharp regression verifies the same filter, including exclusion of a JSONL header with no cwd.

Pinned direct CLI resolution accepts case-sensitive exact ID and ID prefixes; the interactive selector performs case-insensitive fuzzy text search over ID, name, first-message text and CWD. PiSharp's /resume exact-name lookup is an added convenience; its tested ID-prefix behavior now matches Pi. Default-directory discovery includes sessions without stored cwd; PiSharp uses the current store's working directory fallback. Project-context rebinding is covered separately by the cross-project RPC process fixture. Reverse trust transitions and provider-catalog rebinding remain open.

The exact-pin oracle confirms Pi list streams a valid 1,048,769-byte header while findMostRecentSession ignores that candidate after its 1 MiB header scan and falls back to the next session. PiSharp accepts that header within its stricter 16 MiB record and 128 MiB whole-file bounds; this API-specific bounded-read difference is explicitly classified, not counted as a strict match.
